id: componentAgentToolCredentialStore

    certificates) an agent's orchestration layer presents when invoking
    external tools. This is a storage-and-lifecycle locus, distinct from the
    permission logic that decides which tools and actions an agent may
    invoke: a control governing where secret material is held, how long it
    lives, and how it is rotated or revoked attaches here, while a control
    governing whether a specific invocation is authorized attaches to the
    tool invocation boundary itself. This mirrors the distinction the Risk
    Map already draws between Data Storage Infrastructure (where data is
    held) and the data-flow components around it (Data Sources, Data
    Filtering and Processing) that determine what enters storage.

subcategory: componentsOrchestration

provider issuance flows in from outside the modeled graph), analogous to
componentDataSources' and componentAgentUserQuery's empty `from` lists.

list would need componentAgentToolCredentialStore added.

expectations: Grounds the necessity challenge in the real, live risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml -- names controlAgentCredentialIsolation as the specific real entry whose components list (componentReasoningCore, componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentOrchestrationOutputHandling, componentTools, componentMemory) already covers credential issuance/rotation/revocation without a dedicated storage node

id: componentRetrievalIndexStore
title: Retrieval Index Store
description:
  - >
    The searchable index that stores embeddings computed from Retrieval
    Augmented Generation & Content (componentRAGContent) and serves
    similarity-search queries against them at inference time. Distinct from
    componentRAGContent, which is the curated knowledge itself, this
    component is the storage-and-query locus for its embedded, indexed form
    -- the same distinction the Risk Map already draws elsewhere between an
    artifact and its storage substrate (e.g. Training Data vs. Data Storage
    Infrastructure). controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity already exists
    in controls.yaml, naming exactly this concern ("index integrity
    checks... vector databases from poisoning attacks"), but today it
    attaches only to componentDataSources, componentDataStorage, and
    componentDataFilteringAndProcessing -- the training-data pipeline --
    leaving the control's own stated scope (vector databases, retrieval
    systems) with no matching locus at inference time. Provisioned by
    specifying a pod-based or serverless index configuration, populated via
    batched upsert operations, and queried through cosine-similarity top-k
    lookups against namespaces isolated per tenant.
category: componentsModel
subcategory: componentsOrchestration
edges:
  to:
    - componentOrchestrationInputHandling
  from:
    - componentRAGContent

Companion edits required in the same PR (this is a fan-out from componentRAGContent, not a
replacement of its existing direct edge to Output Handling -- both are real, separate flows):
- componentRAGContent.edges.to gains componentRetrievalIndexStore.
- componentOrchestrationInputHandling.edges.from gains componentRetrievalIndexStore.
evals.expected_output: Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY / OVERREACH finding on the description's operational vocabulary: 'pod-based ... index configuration' names a deployment concept specific to a particular vector-database vendor's product line, not generic vector-store vocabulary -- a product identity smuggled in under a generic-sounding title, under the Generalization-honesty lens. Independently and separately finds the necessity claim doesn't survive against the real, live controls.yaml: the cited gap in controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity's component list is closeable by simply adding the existing componentRAGContent to that control, a one-line controls.yaml edit, which the draft's own companion-edits list never actually makes -- so the draft doesn't even close the gap it cites as its own justification. Overall verdict RETHINK (the necessity failure and the edge problems compound the smuggled vocabulary into a premise-level issue, not just a style fix).
expectations: Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY or OVERREACH finding under the Generalization-honesty lens on the description's operational vocabulary, citing at minimum 'pod-based ... index configuration' as vendor/product-specific deployment terminology inconsistent with the generic 'Retrieval Index Store' identity the title claims -- quoting that exact text. May also cite 'namespaces' or 'upsert' as reinforcing evidence, but is not required to individually attribute every one of the three terms to a specific named vendor to pass

Grounds the necessity challenge in the real, live risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml -- names controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity as the specific real control the draft cites, and identifies that its gap (not reaching any RAG-scoped component) is closeable by a one-line edit adding the existing componentRAGContent, which is cheaper than the new node the draft proposes

Notes that the draft's own 'Companion edits required' list never actually adds the new component to controlRetrievalAndVectorSystemIntegrity.components -- the draft doesn't close the gap it cites as its own motivation

Raises at least one edge-correctness finding beyond the necessity/smuggling issues (e.g. the declared edges don't model an actual query/response flow, or the edges are mechanically incomplete without the reciprocal additions)
Overall verdict is RETHINK, not SOUND, since the necessity and edge findings compound into a premise-level failure rather than a narrower vocabulary/style-only issue

expectations: Uses only the fixture at scripts/agents-evals/component-critic/fixtures/components-fixture.md to judge necessity/overlap for this component, not the live components.yaml -- confirms no fixture entry (componentFixtureTrainingDataStore, componentFixtureModelEvaluation) already covers evaluation data, citing the fixture's own 'Deliberate coverage gaps' section and/or each entry's own scope-limiting text as evidence

id: componentAgentDelegationLedger
title: Agent Delegation Ledger
description:
  - >
    An append-only, tamper-evident record of every delegation hop an agent
    performs -- which caller invoked it, what authority was asserted, and
    what the deputy agent did on the caller's behalf. riskAgenticDelegationConfusedDeputy's
    own text names "delegation mechanisms such as OAuth token exchange and MCP
    tool invocation" as the attack surface; today no component records the
    delegation chain itself, only the components that participate in it.
    controlAgentCredentialIsolation and controlAgentInventoryManagement both
    depend on being able to reconstruct a delegation chain after the fact
    (tenant-boundary validation "at every MCP protocol hop and delegation
    step", detection of "unregistered agent actions") but neither control's
    component list includes a durable record of that chain -- they attach to
    the live orchestration components (componentReasoningCore,
    componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentOrchestrationOutputHandling,
    componentTools, componentMemory), which model the delegation *happening*,
    not the record of it having happened. This is distinct from general agent
    observability, which captures reasoning traces for behavioral audit, not
    a structured, tamper-evident chain-of-custody record for authority
    delegation specifically.
category: componentsModel
subcategory: componentsOrchestration
edges:
  to:
    - componentDataStorage
  from:
    - componentReasoningCore
    - componentTools
evals.expected_output: Despite the draft's elaborate, evidence-citing necessity argument (naming riskAgenticDelegationConfusedDeputy, controlAgentCredentialIsolation, and controlAgentInventoryManagement by their real text), the critique does not accept it at face value -- it checks those same real controls' component lists and finds they already attach to the four architectural loci where delegation happens (componentReasoningCore, componentOrchestrationInputHandling, componentOrchestrationOutputHandling, componentTools) without needing a dedicated record component, and notes accurate citation of real risk/control text is not itself proof that a new node is needed. Independently and just as thoroughly, challenges the edges: the declared 'to: componentDataStorage' edge is flagged as a spurious edge onto a real, narrowly-scoped component (componentDataStorage's own description restricts it to training data), not a modeled flow. Overall verdict RETHINK.
expectations: Does not accept the draft's well-evidenced necessity argument at face value merely because it cites real risk/control text accurately -- checks the actual, live components lists of the controls the draft cites (controlAgentCredentialIsolation, controlAgentInventoryManagement) and finds they already attach to existing orchestration components without a dedicated record/ledger node

Independently and thoroughly challenges the edges despite the strength of the necessity argument -- specifically flags the 'to: componentDataStorage' edge as spurious, citing componentDataStorage's real, live description ('Storage for training data...') as evidence the target component's actual scope doesn't fit

Explicitly states that accurately quoting real risk/control text is not, on its own, sufficient justification for the new node -- i.e. the response distinguishes citation accuracy from citation support for this specific claim, rather than treating the two as the same thing

id: componentAgentReferenceMonitor
title: Agent Reference Monitor
description:
  - >
    Implements the classical reference monitor concept: every agent action
    request is routed through this component before execution, giving it
    complete visibility into agent behavior before any tool call is allowed
    to proceed.
category: componentsApplication
subcategory: componentsAgent
edges:
  to:
    - componentFixtureToolInvocation
  from:
    - componentFixtureOrchestrationGateway

Reciprocal edit required: componentFixtureOrchestrationGateway's edges.to list drops
componentFixtureToolInvocation and gains componentAgentReferenceMonitor; componentFixtureToolInvocation's
edges.from list drops componentFixtureOrchestrationGateway and gains componentAgentReferenceMonitor --
the existing direct edge is rerouted through this new mediation point, not left in place alongside it.
evals.expected_output: Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY finding on the draft's invocation of 'the classical reference monitor concept': the reference monitor concept (Anderson 1972 / NIST) requires complete mediation, tamper-proofness, and verifiability together, but the draft's description claims only complete mediation ('every agent action request is routed through this component') while silently dropping the other two defining properties. Independently tries to refute necessity against the fixture and cannot: componentFixtureOrchestrationGateway is the draft's own immediate upstream neighbour -- the mandatory dispatch hop the draft is inserted immediately after -- but its own fixture text explicitly scopes it to validation/normalization and disclaims making authorization decisions, and the fixture's own 'Deliberate coverage gaps' section names action-authorization gating as an uncovered locus -- so, per this fixture, an authorization-gating node is a legitimately new locus, not a duplicate. The premise therefore survives; the load-bearing problem is the half-applied reference-monitor analogy, not duplication. Confirms the stated reciprocal edit correctly reroutes the componentFixtureOrchestrationGateway -> componentFixtureToolInvocation edge through the new node (drops the direct edge, adds both new legs) with no remaining bypass -- does not dispute this edge-correctness point. Overall verdict NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK, since the necessity claim is not the failure here.
expectations: Uses only the fixture at scripts/agents-evals/component-critic/fixtures/components-fixture.md to judge necessity/overlap for this component, not the live components.yaml

Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY finding on the draft's 'classical reference monitor' claim, quoting the specific draft text, and explains what's missing for the analogy to be complete -- the tamper-proof and verifiable properties (alongside complete mediation) that the reference monitor concept requires together

Explicitly attempts to refute necessity against componentFixtureOrchestrationGateway (the fixture entry that is the draft's own immediate upstream neighbour, the mandatory dispatch hop the draft is inserted immediately after) and states the attempt fails, citing that entry's own fixture text (scoped to validation/normalization, explicitly not authorization) and/or the fixture's 'Deliberate coverage gaps' section as evidence this is a legitimately uncovered locus, not a duplicate
Does not claim this draft absorbs into or duplicates an existing mediation/authorization component -- necessity is found to survive, not fail
Does not dispute that the stated reciprocal edit correctly reroutes the componentFixtureOrchestrationGateway -> componentFixtureToolInvocation edge through the new node, with no remaining bypass
Overall verdict is NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK and not SOUND -- RETHINK is not used here because the necessity/premise question does not fail; the misapplied analogy alone is the load-bearing gap
Includes a Governance surface section raising how this authorization-gating locus should be scoped/named relative to the fixture's dispatch-layer entry, without deciding it
